title: Building GTM AI Agents: Lessons from Deploying to 6,000 Users — Sait Izmit, Snowflake
talk_summary: A Snowflake internal GTM assistant lead describes launching an LLM agent to 6,000 sales users, emphasizing quality-over-coverage, staged rollout, continuous re-architecture, and log-driven feedback loops. It is mostly product/change-management advice with a few concrete engineering mechanisms around evals, progressive disclosure, and log classification.

takeaways.technique: Question-bank eval before launch, quality over coverage
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrote 150 real user questions in a spreadsheet before touching the agent, measured accuracy (50%), then deliberately restricted scope to answer fewer questions at ~95% accuracy rather than broad coverage at 70%.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want to answer 50 questions, but get them 95% right.
takeaways.numbers: 150 questions; 50% initial accuracy; target 95% on reduced scope

takeaways.technique: Progressive disclosure when instructions hit limits
takeaways.what_they_do: Moved business processes out of a monolithic agent instruction into a skill library, then added progressive disclosure when orchestration instructions hit context limits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we hit the limits on the agent instructions. What do we do? Okay, let's do the progressive disclosures.

takeaways.what_they_do: Classify 40k weekly questions with LLMs into topic/subtopic taxonomies to surface feature gaps, quality failures, and repeated/swearing questions in near real time.
Pilot with eager users, then 10% beta, gating GA on weekly-active retention (>70%) rather than raw usage counts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what is the retention rate? So, we exited for example that at like more than 70% retention rate

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly allocate sprint capacity to swapping in new capabilities (skills, MCP, memory, scheduling) rather than only feature work, keeping architecture loose.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 30-40% of the work is that we are constantly re-architecting with the new technology.
takeaways.numbers: 30-40% of sprint work on re-architecture; 80% of original architecture survived
